title: Reece James Injury: Progress, Potential Return Date for Chelsea Star
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 10, 2026Reece James is set for a spell on the sidelines. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images Chelsea have been faced with a handful of injury issues during the first few months of the season, with Reece James the latest to be forced into a spell on the sidelines.

James was unable to represent England during the international action as Thomas Tuchel confirmed the Chelsea captain wasn’t included in his roster due to injury. The 26-year-old also missed Chelsea’s defeat against Brentford right before the international break and sat out the 5–1 win over Bournemouth immediately after.
A final verdict on his fitness is in, and unfortunately for Chelsea, the news is not good.

Reece James is Chelsea’s leader. / Chris Lee/Chelsea FC/Getty Images Alonso was the first to reveal James had suffered a knee injury during training. After being sent for scans, it was subsequently decided that surgery was the only option.

Chelsea did describe the process as “minor,” which initially offered some relief to fans fearing his season may already be over, but no formal details about the injury have been revealed at this point.
Knee injuries have not been common in James’s career thus far. He has battled hamstring problems on a number of occasions, giving him an unwanted reputation in the process.

Reece James has struggled to remain fit throughout his career.  / Vince Mignott/MB Media/Getty Images When Chelsea confirmed James’s surgery, they did not offer a timeframe for his return. Blues boss Alonso had said he would be assessed “week by week,” but it soon became clear that would not be possible.

Indeed, reports quickly put an estimate of three months on James’s recovery, which may well be more of a reflection on the need to proceed with the utmost caution when it comes to a player with his difficult injury record.

“We don’t have the exact, it will be several weeks for sure, it’s not going to be short,” Alonso said. “It's not going to be two, three weeks things, it’s going to be longer and after we will see before Christmas, after Christmas time will tell but things have to be done properly, that he feels right and that needs in the best possible condition.
“A disappointment for everyone, for him but we need to ... we have a squad to follow that to deal with the injuries.”

Jordan Henderson scored a brace in his home Chelsea debut.  / Chris Lee/Chelsea FC/Getty Images     James has operated almost exclusively as a central midfielder in the infancy of the Alonso era. Fortunately for Chelsea, previously injured midfielders have not only returned to full fitness—they are already producing on the pitch.

Jordan Henderson and Moisés Caicedo formed Alonso’s double-pivot against Bournemouth and thrived, with the pair only recently returning from injury themselves. In his first Chelsea start at Stamford Bridge, Henderson scored a brace and picked up an assist, while Caicedo looked solid in his first start of the campaign.
Alonso was delighted with how his starting midfielders performed, and Roméo Lavia also looked sharp during his cameo after suffering an injury scare during the international break.

If Alonso also needs cover at right-center back or wingback—positions James can also operate in—Josh Acheampong and Pedro Neto have both impressed this season. Furthermore, summer recruit Marco Palestra is back available after starting his debut season with his own fitness concern.
